surface_summary: The Corbin family is thrown into turmoil when the famous family necklace is reported stolen from a supposedly locked safe. An imitation necklace is returned mysteriously, and suspicions arise among family members and guests, with accusations flying and a secret elopement complicating matters.
accepted_facts: The necklace was stolen from the safe at The Oaks
An imitation necklace was returned to the grandmother's room
Punch Corbin saw a man in pajamas moving in the house at night
Judy Corbin eloped with Bill Grant and planned to marry him secretly
inferred_conclusions: Victoria Ashcroft Corbin was innocent and only worried about the family
Bill Grant was the thief who stole the necklace
Bruce Applebury was unaware of the necklace's true status and innocent
mechanism_description: Victoria Ashcroft Corbin, facing financial difficulties, had the real necklace pawned and secretly replaced it with a perfect imitation. The thief, Raglan, hired as a window shade hanger, hid in the house in pajamas and stole the imitation necklace from the safe during a moment when the house was distracted. Upon discovering it was a fake, he returned it to the grandmother's room to mislead the family and avoid suspicion. The real necklace was kept by Bruce Applebury, who was unaware of the substitution.
delivery_path: Victoria arranges for an imitation necklace to be made and pawns the real one
Raglan is hired to work in the house and conceals himself in a trunk room
During a lunch break, Raglan steals the imitation necklace from the unlocked safe
Raglan discovers the necklace is fake and returns it to the grandmother's room
Bruce Applebury retrieves the real necklace from the bank and keeps it
Judy and Bill Grant elope and plan to marry secretly to avoid scandal
The family confronts the situation leading to the exposure of Raglan and resolution
outcome_result: The real necklace is recovered, the thief Raglan is caught, and Judy marries Bill Grant with the family's reluctant blessing.

false_assumption.statement: The necklace was stolen by an insider during the wedding preparations.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Multiple family members had access and motives, and the safe was found unlocked. Suspicious behavior by family members and guests suggested an inside job.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The actual thief was an outsider hiding in the house, and the real necklace had been pawned and replaced with an imitation.

supporting_points: Bill was seen entering Bruce's room at night
He avoided discussing the necklace openly
He was in a hurry to get a marriage license
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Bill had no motive to steal and was trusted by Judy; the real thief was an outsider

red_herrings.description: Bill Grant's secretive behavior and elopement with Judy suggested he might have stolen the necklace.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Bill was protecting Judy and had no motive to steal; he was helping her escape an unwanted marriage.

red_herrings.description: Bruce Applebury accused his cousin Bill Grant of stealing the necklace, fueling suspicion.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Bruce's accusation was driven by anger and misunderstanding; the necklace was stolen by Raglan.

closed_circle.rationale: All these individuals had access to the house and the necklace during the relevant times, and the mystery was confined to the household and its immediate guests.

time_anchors: Wednesday afternoon when Mrs. Corbin showed the necklace
Thursday afternoon when the imitation necklace was stolen
Night of the theft and return of the imitation necklace
Early morning when Judy and Bill eloped
Morning of the wedding day when the real necklace was stolen from Bruce
time_windows: Lunch hour Thursday when servants were away
Night hours when guests were asleep
Morning before dawn when Judy and Bill left
access_objects: The safe in grandmother's sitting room
Trunk closet on the top floor

The empty morocco box found by Judy and Punch

inference_path.effect: Victoria is the mastermind behind the substitution and theft.

Bank documents or notes about the pawn transaction

inference_path.correction: Their elopement was to avoid scandal and family conflict.
inference_path.effect: Judy's behavior was motivated by family pressures, not theft.

Judy and Bill's conversation with the narrator

inference_path.observation: Raglan confessed and returned the real necklace.
inference_path.correction: Raglan was caught hiding in the house and surrendered.
inference_path.effect: The theft was solved by uncovering the outsider thief.

Recovery of the real necklace from Raglan's possession

discriminating_test.design: Recreate the timeline of the necklace's disappearance and return by tracking the movements of all suspects and witnesses during the critical hours. Verify the presence of the man in pajamas and the accessibility of the safe and rooms. Confirm the identity of the pajamas and the hiding place of the thief.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals that only an outsider disguised in pajamas could have stolen and returned the imitation necklace without detection, and that the real necklace was pawned and kept by Bruce.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The test passes if the pajamas with the tear are matched to Raglan and the safe's access times align with his presence, excluding all family members as the thief.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed accounts of the necklace's whereabouts, the characters' movements, and the discovery of the pajamas with the tear. Punch's observations and Mr. Smith's expert analysis provide clues to the thief's identity. The false accusations and red herrings are clearly presented and later refuted, allowing the attentive reader to deduce the true mechanism.
